scope: All 18 original lead source-first findings for chunk 16 compared individually with actual draft parent meanings and stance and already item-reviewed component dispositions. This is source-first reconciliation, not new full-record or repaired-value approval.

rows.source_first_requirement: Doyle presents a constituency that valued equality and property gains but tired of war and political mobilization. Enduring settlement required calm; Bonaparte’s success involved sacrificing many 1789 principles, not straightforward fulfillment of all of them.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The ending and property-security parents preserve desired stability and the costs in representation. Keep social beneficiaries’ fatigue distinct from approval of every revolutionary government; neither the official proclamation nor later peace alone is the entire ending.

rows.source_first_requirement: Voters rejected endorsed candidates despite very low participation; Councils largely accepted majority returns and then purged the Directory. Sieyès used cross-faction constitutional resentment to concentrate executive power, contrary to some supporters’ expectations.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The election, Prairial and Sieyes parents retain the reversed direction of this coup: legislature purged executive. Keep very low turnout and accepted majority returns, and distinguish broad constitutional resentment from Sieyes’s stronger-executive objective; this is 1799, not Prairial 1795.

rows.source_first_requirement: Manège and a revived press accompanied full conscription, forced loan and Law of Hostages. The last allowed sanctions against relatives without proven complicity. Memories of Year II helped Sieyès and Fouché suppress the revival.
rows.independent_reconciliation: Distinct Jacobin, military and civil-emergency parents preserve the measures and backlash. Keep the Hostage Law’s liability without proven complicity separate from the forced loan, and conscription separate from both. Fouché/Sieyes containment belongs in the revival’s specific final phase.

rows.source_first_requirement: Toulouse resisted a royalist peasant rising while Sieyès suppressed the left. Jourdan’s country-in-danger motion failed. Allied divisions enabled victories in Holland/Switzerland; western chouannerie resumed amid conscription anxiety.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The Toulouse, coalition-recovery and western-resistance parents retain different threats. Preserve the failed country-in-danger motion, political embarrassment after republican defence, allied divisions and renewed chouannerie; suppressing the left did not eliminate right-wing revolt.

rows.source_first_requirement: Sieyès needed a general for extra-constitutional change; Bonaparte exploited the opportunity. Lucien, Fouché and Talleyrand helped. Removal to Saint-Cloud, executive collapse, legislative resistance and military expulsion preceded provisional consuls.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The coup and alliance parents preserve planning and improvisation, the Saint-Cloud transfer and military expulsion after chamber resistance. Retain Lucien, Fouché and Talleyrand’s roles and pretext versus proven conspiracy; preserve the rendered 374–376 chronology discrepancy.

rows.source_first_requirement: Doyle argues elections never operated freely and rulers failed to accept legitimate parties/opposition, but also recognizes opponents’ restoration aims or terroristic rhetoric and likely intolerance. Bonaparte and Sieyès proposed different executive remedies.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The political-culture diagnosis survives across the parents. Retain genuine threat and opponents’ likely intolerance as qualifications, while not treating the constitution as mechanically doomed or Sieyes’s proposed executive as identical to Bonaparte’s adopted supremacy.

rows.source_first_requirement: Tiered lists selected eligible citizens; Senate chose legislators. Tribunate debated without voting, Legislative Body voted without debate, and only government initiated laws via Council of State. Bonaparte rejected Sieyès’s Grand Elector plan for dominant First Consul power.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The institutional parent preserves tiered eligibility lists, Senate selection, divided debate/voting and executive initiative via the Council of State. Final parent fields must also distinguish the proposed Grand Elector and the Senate’s intended legality check from adopted powers and later obscurity.

rows.source_first_requirement: Approval figures were inflated amid large abstention and implementation preceded the result. Official claims to preserve original principles are not Doyle’s unqualified evaluation; stability remained to be achieved.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The constitution parent explicitly retains manipulated returns, abstention and implementation before ratification. The end-of-Revolution proclamation remains an official claim whose substantive conditions were not yet all achieved; no universal-consent inference is warranted.

rows.source_first_requirement: Russian withdrawal weakened the coalition. Marengo narrowly escaped defeat; Moreau’s Hohenlinden victory forced peace. Lunéville and Amiens consolidated gains while colonial and commercial concessions differed. These settlements were central to domestic legitimacy.
rows.independent_reconciliation: Distinct campaign and treaty parents preserve Russian withdrawal, narrow Marengo recovery and Moreau’s decisive Hohenlinden victory. Keep domestic legitimacy and separate continental/colonial concessions; victorious peace was neither solely Bonaparte’s battlefield work nor permanent.

rows.source_first_requirement: Etruria’s Bourbon kingdom, recognition of Naples and Spanish cession of Louisiana show altered regime priorities; Parthenopean restoration was abandoned. France could exact more from allies than enemies.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The settlement and hegemony parents must explicitly preserve Etruria’s Bourbon kingdom, accommodation with Naples instead of restoring the Parthenopean Republic, and Louisiana’s acquisition through Spain. This pragmatic dynastic accommodation was not wholesale old-regime restoration.

rows.source_first_requirement: British naval victories, Malta, armed neutrality and Copenhagen left sea power intact but could not reverse French continental domination. War weariness and political change made Amiens possible on strongly French-favouring terms.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The maritime and Amiens parents preserve British sea strength alongside continental inability, domestic strain and the shift to negotiation. Retain Malta, armed neutrality, Copenhagen, Pitt/Addington and transient peace as distinct routes, not proof of a French naval victory.

rows.source_first_requirement: Some hoped Bonaparte would act as a French Monck. He delayed rejecting Louis XVIII, pacified chouan leaders through conciliation and coercion, then guaranteed revolutionary property while allowing émigré return. Cadoudal remained hostile.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The royalist and property parents retain strategic ambiguity, delayed rejection, chouan coercion/conciliation and conditional émigré reconciliation. Keep Cadoudal’s continuing hostility and legal/practical amnesty distinctions; revolutionary purchasers were protected rather than dispossessed for returned émigrés.

rows.source_first_requirement: Cadoudal’s chouans caused the bombing, yet Bonaparte used it against Jacobins despite police proof. Deportations and executions also aimed to reassure property owners.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The bombing parent explicitly retains actual chouan culpability and deliberate punishment of uninvolved Jacobins despite police evidence. This attribution and instrumental repression are essential distinctions, not optional actor aliases.

rows.source_first_requirement: Repeal of coercive laws, Bank of France, cash debt service, tax collection, prefects and special courts projected stability. Conscription evasion fed brigandage; returning troops enabled suppression. A Civil Code drew on older projects and clarified property law.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The fiscal, administrative and legal parents preserve concrete mechanisms. Retain uncertain fiscal foundations, pre-existing code projects, conscription-linked brigandage, released troops and special justice. Everyday security must coexist with arbitrary high-level punishment; only the two civil emergency laws were repealed.

rows.source_first_requirement: Church-state conflict had broken early consensus. Bonaparte regarded religion pragmatically as support for order, while Pius VII’s accommodation of equality made negotiation possible. Reconciliation could separate religious allegiance from counter-revolution.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The religious-policy and Concordat parents preserve political pragmatism, Pius VII’s willingness to reconcile Christianity with equality, and the aim of separating religion from counter-revolution. Do not infer personal belief from Bonaparte’s gestures or reduce negotiation to papal capitulation.

rows.source_first_requirement: Catholicism was recognized as majority religion with freedom of worship retained; bishops were state-nominated and papally invested, clergy publicly supported and obedient. Church lands were not restored, though papal acceptance did not concede legality of confiscation.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The Concordat parent retains majority religion, freedom of belief, public support and divided state nomination/papal investiture. Preserve practical acceptance of non-return without papal endorsement of confiscation or annexation; majority status is not exclusive dominant state religion.

rows.source_first_requirement: All old bishops were displaced; Tam multa and papal deprivation expanded recognized authority. Some constitutional bishops returned. Unilateral Organic Articles restricted papal communication and revived Gallican teaching, producing a mixed settlement rather than simple ultramontane victory.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The Organic Articles and Concordat parents preserve mixed episcopal reconstitution and the tension between strengthened papal recognition and unilateral Gallican controls. Keep resignation, deprivation and fresh appointment separate; the settlement is not unqualified ultramontane victory.

rows.source_first_requirement: Experienced nominated legislators still criticized policy. Senate removal of opponents used ambiguous renewal provisions before Concordat enactment; independent press loss limits public-reaction evidence. Consul for life and Easter celebrations marked stability secured at representative freedom’s expense.
rows.independent_reconciliation: The purge and constitutional parents preserve ambiguous renewal rules, Senate action and removal of opposition before the religious enactment. Retain press suppression as a limit on evidence, police reports as qualified, the Year X/calendar discrepancy, and representative costs of life-consul consolidation.
